speaker: Priya
text: Okay, sprint planning. Full agenda today: two course corrections and one green light. Let's not make this a two-hour meeting.

speaker: Priya
text: It's data, not drama. Sam, give them the cache numbers first.

speaker: Sam
text: So, the benchmark surprised me. I replayed a full week of ingestion traffic, and the hot set is about sixty megabytes. Sixty. Redis handles it fine, but we'd be operating an entire extra service to cache something that fits in process memory.

speaker: Priya
text: Right. So here's the call: Redis is overkill for v1 — we're going with an in-memory LRU instead. I'm taking the cache work off Sam's plate so he can help Marco, and the new target is August 14.

speaker: Sam
text: Honestly? Relieved. One less service on my pager. I'll hand the branch over by Wednesday.

speaker: Chen
text: Hold on — which ticket is that, the ingestion one? The add-cache-layer one?

speaker: Priya
text: That's the one, the cache layer ticket. I'll update it after this. Okay, Marco — your turn. The auth news.

speaker: Marco
text: Auth0 finally sent the enterprise quote, and it's four times what we budgeted. Four. Times. So we're dropping Auth0 and going with Clerk — same OAuth2 flows at a fraction of the price — and the cutover moves to September 1.

speaker: Sam
text: Do they have parity on the enterprise SSO piece? That was the whole reason we—

speaker: Marco
text: They do. I ran our whole claims-mapping doc against their API last night. We lose nothing except the invoice.

speaker: Chen
text: Last thing — the offline spec I've been drafting since kickoff is done. Sync strategy, conflict handling, storage budget, the lot. It's in the shared drive and Sam and Marco already left comments.

speaker: Priya
text: I read it this morning, and it's exactly what we scoped at kickoff. The spec is approved as written — offline mode build starts next sprint with Chen leading. No change to anything we agreed in July.
